YOU are nearest puck; D1 is inside with Gold 1 approaching slot.

questions.prompt: What is the puck state?
questions.explanation: The puck marker is loose, so YOU read a retrieval race while D1 protects inside; if control changes, roles update.

questions.prompt: Which two jobs need separating?
questions.explanation: The nearest player attacks puck while inside defender protects danger; two at wall exposes slot.

questions.prompt: Arrange one failed-clear recovery.

options.text: YOU retrieve if lane is reachable

questions.explanation: The call shares information; nearest route decides retrieval; D1’s inside position prevents free slot attack.

questions.prompt: Move D1 between Gold 1 and the Navy net while YOU attack wall puck.
questions.explanation: D1’s net-side spot protects slot and leaves YOU a retrieval lane; if Gold 1 wins puck, D1 becomes carrier defender.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 gains clear control, what changes?

options.text: D1 contains new carrier while YOU recover next inside lane
Both defenders remain tied to wall

questions.explanation: Clear control changes puck threat, so D1’s coverage and YOU’s recovery update; if Navy recovers, rebuild support.

questions.prompt: Why is a failed clear a role-change moment?
questions.explanation: The blocked puck removes assumption of exit, so one retrieves and another protects slot; if possession becomes clear, both jobs change.

sourceChecks.scope: Read via WebFetch + direct PDF pages 7-8 extraction. Confirmed this is Hockey Canada's Program of Excellence (elite U17/national-team level, (c) 2008), not a U13 document. Pages 7-8 state the four offensive/defensive team-play principles (Pressure, Puck Control/Stall-Contain, Support, Transition) and define 'Support - Offensive' (teammates away from the puck must be available as passing options) and 'Transition - Offensive' (moving quickly from defense to attack once the puck is recovered).
